extracted.intended_audience: tourists and locals looking for things to do in Hollywood (movie buffs, foodies, families, and general visitors)
extracted.subtask_description: A short travel-list style guide recommending iconic, historic, culinary, and entertainment-focused activities to do in Hollywood, with practical notes and locations. The page selects items that appeal to movie fans, foodies, and visitors seeking scenic views or live entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconic / landmark status
rubrics_metrics.description: Include places that are widely recognized as emblematic of Hollywood (e.g., the Hollywood Walk of Fame, the Hollywood Sign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article repeatedly highlights 'iconic landmarks like the Hollywood Walk of Fame and the Hollywood Sign' and frames these as primary reasons to visit—choose sites with strong name recognition and cultural cachet (Chinese Theater, Hollywood Sign, Walk of Fame, Yamashiro, Universal Studios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection to film and entertainment culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize activities tied to the film industry or cinematic history (e.g., theaters, studio tours, cemeteries with film legends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes 'most of the things to do are related to the film industry' and recommends attending film-adjacent experiences such as the Chinese Theater (IMAX, handprints), Universal Studios (Studio Tour), and free outdoor movie screenings at Hollywood Forever Cemetery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and cultural significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Select sites with historical, architectural, or cultural importance (e.g., Musso & Frank, Hollyhock House, Hollywood Forever Cemetery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Frank Lloyd Wright's Hollyhock House and century-old Musso & Frank; the article uses history and heritage as reasons these places are 'must-see' and frames them as cultural treasures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and expectation management
rubrics_metrics.description: Set realistic expectations about what Hollywood actually is versus TV/film portrayals (glamour vs. reality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide warns: 'If you’re looking for a glamorous or ‘movie-like’ experience, this part of the city might disappoint you.' It contrasts actual Hollywood with Beverly Hills/Rodeo Drive for those seeking mansions and luxury, advising readers to pick activities accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free or low-cost experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight complimentary or budget-friendly activities available to visitors (e.g., free self-guided tours, free outdoor movie screenings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article calls out 'self-guided tour, for free' at Hollywood Forever Cemetery and describes free outdoor movie screenings as a cherished tradition—use cost as a selection factor when listing things to do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenic viewpoints and photo opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Include places offering strong vistas or iconic photo backdrops (e.g., Lake Hollywood Park, Sunset Ranch, Ovation Hollywood vantage points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 'Get amazing views of the Hollywood sign' the guide recommends specific vantage points (Ovation Hollywood, Beachwood Drive, Lake Hollywood Park, Sunset Ranch) and emphasizes 360-degree cityscape views—prioritize spots with recommended vantage points and sunset timing tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culinary distinctiveness and local food/beverage offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature eateries and beverage spots that offer authentic or standout local flavors (e.g., Nam Coffee, Musso & Frank, Tabula Rasa, Courage Bagels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights provenance (Nam Coffee's Vietnamese roots), longevity and classic menus (Musso & Frank), concise but impressive wine lists (Tabula Rasa), and signature products plus waittimes (Courage Bagels). Use origin stories, signature dishes, and queue patience as evaluation points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live performance and comedy scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend venues with regular live shows or training/performance opportunities (e.g., UCB for improv, sketch, stand-up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide frames UCB as 'this comedy institution and training center' and a hub for new talent—emphasize variety of performances (improv, sketch, stand-up), institutional reputation, and suitability for a night out with friends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique or novel experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Include activities that are unusual or distinctive to the area (e.g., horseback riding to the Hollywood sign, the pagoda at Yamashiro).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recommends horseback rides at Sunset Ranch and notes Yamashiro's 14th-century-style pagoda—these items are chosen for experiential novelty and should be highlighted as memorable, non-typical tourist activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event programming and seasonal offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Select sites that host recurring events (e.g., alfresco cinema nights, wine tastings, cultural events at Hollyhock House).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hollyhock House 'hosts a variety of alfresco cinema nights, wine tastings, and cultural events'—use event programming to indicate times when a visit is especially worthwhile and to signal family or social appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowd, queue, and practical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag high-traffic sites and potential downsides like crowds and long lines (e.g., Chinese Theater crowds, Walk of Fame packed, Courage Bagels queues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide repeatedly mentions 'bustling crowd of vendors and visitors,' 'usually packed' Walk of Fame, and long queues at Courage Bagels—advise patience, timing strategies, or alternatives when recommending these places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelessness / longevity as a selling point
rubrics_metrics.description: Value establishments or landmarks with longstanding reputations (e.g., Musso & Frank 'for over a century', Hollywood sign since 1923).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article uses age and storied past to justify inclusion—presenting places as enduring parts of Hollywood's identity increases their appeal to visitors seeking authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for different visitor types (movie buffs, foodies, families)
rubrics_metrics.description: Match activities to audience interests—film buff attractions, foodie stops, family-friendly parks and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece explicitly says 'Whether you’re a movie buff, a foodie, or simply looking for a fun and dynamic atmosphere, Hollywood offers something for everyone' and tailors entries (studio tours for film buffs, bagels/wine/dining for foodies, parks/events for families).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and proximity for further exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how a site’s location fits into broader Los Angeles exploration (convenient location for exploring other parts of Los Angeles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Is Hollywood... worth visiting?' section notes Hollywood's 'convenient location for exploring other parts of Los Angeles'—use geographic convenience when recommending itineraries or grouped activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere and vibe (e.g., minimalist, industrial, cozy, timeless charm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the venue's mood to set visitor expectations (e.g., Tabula Rasa's 'minimalist, industrial vibe', Musso & Frank's 'timeless charm').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article uses ambiance descriptors to indicate whether a spot is relaxed, historic, or lively—include these cues so readers can match activities to the mood they want (date-night, casual, historic).
